author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose a PS2 image that appears under the wrong library title
summary: Compare detected serial, physical-disc record, dump log, executable region, filename, hash, and metadata source to decide whether the fault belongs to presentation, identity, or the working image.
heroAlt: ImgBurn source-drive screen showing disc identity before a PS2 image is named and added to a library

blocks.text: Separate the displayed label from the detected executable

A filename can be wrong while the image bytes and detected serial are correct. Conversely, a polished cover and title can hide a different region or revision. Diagnose from strongest evidence outward: owned disc, dump log, independent hash, detected serial, cold-boot behavior, then filename and downloaded presentation metadata.
Do not rename, patch, redump, or copy saves until the serial and region are established. A save or per-game profile moved to the wrong executable can create a second problem.
Collect identity evidence without modifying the image

items: Physical disc label or private ownership record.
Original dump log and component list.
Current SHA-256 and byte size of the working image.
Detected serial and region from a clean launch.
Current library path, filename, cover, and title captured in a screenshot.

blocks.text: Locate the first disagreement in the evidence chain

items: 1. Compare the working hash with the verified master to rule out a changed or patched copy.
2. Start the image from a clean profile, then capture the disc serial reported by the executable and the library-details screen.
3. Compare that serial and region with the physical label and dump log.
4. If serial agrees but title or cover does not, refresh or correct only presentation metadata.
5. If filename alone is wrong, create a rename ledger and rename the working copy without changing bytes.
6. If serial conflicts with the owned disc record, quarantine the working image and inspect whether folders or source media were mixed.
7. After any presentation or filename fix, refresh once and recheck the profile, favorite, and native save against the verified serial.

blocks.text: Different editions can share localized marketing titles, and compilations can contain executables whose internal labels differ from the package. Preserve both package and executable facts in the private manifest instead of forcing one field to carry every distinction.
The corrected entry should have no unexplained conflict among source, bytes, executable, and presentation.

items: Working hash equals the selected verified master.
Detected serial and region agree with the physical source record.
Filename identifies region or revision where needed.
Cover and displayed title correspond to that exact edition.
Per-game profile and save test target the same serial.

blocks.text: Evidence that points away from metadata

items: Hash differs from master: working bytes changed.
Serial belongs to another disc in the collection: source folders were mixed.
Only a save is rejected: investigate product-code compatibility rather than the cover.
Two entries share one path: overlapping roots or stale scan data must be resolved.

blocks.text: Return to the verified working identity

Restore the working image from the private verified master, restore its previous filename from the ledger, and refresh once with patches disabled. Reapply labels and profiles only after the serial is visible and matches the source record.
Do not publish private dump evidence

A support report can include serial, region, hash, file size, and a redacted log, but not the BIOS, image, keys, or copyrighted disc content. Remove personal filesystem paths from screenshots and logs.
